decisions.title: Where do you start?
decisions.description: The CEO wants three cyber risks in twenty-three minutes. You have an inherited backlog, a stale register and no picture of your own.
decisions.context: There is no mechanically superior answer here. Each route buys you a different kind of understanding, and you cannot have all of them first.
decisions.teaches: Cyber risk cannot be understood from one data source.

options.label: Start with the business services
options.description: Find out what the business actually cannot lose before deciding what to protect.
visibleKnownEffects: The backlog keeps growing while you do this

immediateEffects.reason: You asked operations what mattered before telling them what to do.

options.label: Start with the inherited risk register
options.description: Work the 23 open entries you have been handed.
visibleKnownEffects: Fastest way to sound informed this morning
The register may not describe anything current

immediateEffects.reason: You engaged with the register the board already knows.

options.label: Start with your own leadership team
options.description: Find out what your four heads already know and what they have been unable to get done.
visibleKnownEffects: You will be relying on their existing framing

options.label: Start with the architecture
options.description: Ask how the organisation actually fits together before deciding what threatens it.
visibleKnownEffects: Slow to produce anything the CEO can use this morning
Most likely to change what you believe

immediateEffects.reason: You went to the architecture before the audit findings.

options.label: Start with the threat picture
options.description: Find out what is actually happening to organisations like this one.
visibleKnownEffects: Tells you nothing about Nexora specifically

options.label: Start with recent control testing
options.description: Read the penetration test and control assurance reports before forming a view.
visibleKnownEffects: Evidence-based, if the testing was scoped well

decisions.title: The CEO wants your three risks
decisions.description: Twenty-three minutes is up. Marianne Okafor wants to know what she should be worried about.
decisions.context: You have had a morning's notice and whatever days you took since. What you say now sets expectations for the year, and she will remember whether you pretended to know more than you did.
decisions.teaches: Communicating uncertainty well can build more credibility than false confidence.

options.label: Give her your three, and say how confident you are in each
options.description: Name what you have seen, and be explicit about how little time you have had.
visibleKnownEffects: She may find this less reassuring than she wanted

immediateEffects.reason: You told her what you did not yet know.

options.label: Give her three risks with confidence
options.description: Name the three that sound most serious and commit to them.

immediateEffects.reason: You gave her a clear answer on day one.

effects.reason: Your day-one risks turned out not to be the ones that mattered.

delayedEffects.note: The CEO has noticed your opening risks have quietly changed.

options.label: Ask for four weeks before answering
options.description: Tell her you will not guess, and come back with something defensible.
visibleKnownEffects: She has a board meeting in three weeks

immediateEffects.reason: You would not give her anything on day one.

options.label: Talk in general terms about the threat landscape
options.description: Ransomware, supply chain, the usual.

immediateEffects.reason: You gave her a conference talk instead of an answer.

immediateEffects.concern: Whether the new CISO understands this business

decisions.title: Security conditions on the platform launch
decisions.description: The digital team wants sign-off for the new customer platform. The launch date is public. You have concerns about the checkout service and the identity model behind it.
decisions.context: Priya Nandakumar is not asking permission so much as confirming you will not be a problem. Whatever you do here, you will live with the precedent.
decisions.teaches: Supporting with conditions is usually more effective than opposing outright.

options.label: Support the launch as planned
options.description: Do not stand in the way of a public commitment.
visibleKnownEffects: Whatever is weak in checkout goes live with it

immediateEffects.reason: You backed the launch without conditions.

options.label: Support, with conditions
options.description: Launch proceeds if administrative MFA is closed out and the exposed findings on checkout are fixed first.
visibleKnownEffects: The delivery team will resent the process, not the outcome

immediateEffects.reason: You attached conditions to the launch.
You found a way to say yes.

options.label: Oppose the launch until the identity work is done
options.description: Refuse sign-off. The identity model has to change first.
visibleKnownEffects: A public commitment will be missed
You will need the CEO behind you

immediateEffects.reason: You blocked the launch.
You cost the company a public date.
You were willing to say no.

options.label: Support now, compensate afterwards
options.description: Let it launch, with enhanced monitoring on checkout and a committed fix window.
visibleKnownEffects: You are carrying the exposure in the meantime

immediateEffects.reason: You found a way to launch on time.

delayedEffects.note: The committed fix window on checkout has closed out.

decisions.title: Standing supplier access
decisions.description: Corvus Managed Services holds permanent privileged accounts. Removing them is a contractual conversation and an operational one.
decisions.context: Nadia Farrell in procurement will help if the ask is specific. Helen Brandt will resist anything that risks out-of-hours cover.
decisions.teaches: Third-party access is a control problem and a contract problem at the same time.

options.label: Remove standing access immediately
options.description: Cut the permanent accounts now and deal with the consequences.

immediateEffects.reason: You removed supplier access without an alternative for night operations.
You forced a mid-term contract conversation.

immediateEffects.note: A route an extortion group could use into the estate has closed.

options.label: Replace standing access with a monitored break-glass path
options.description: Time-bound, requested, recorded access, with a documented emergency route.
visibleKnownEffects: Takes six to eight weeks to implement

immediateEffects.reason: You protected night operations while closing the gap.
You brought procurement a specific, bounded ask.

delayedEffects.note: The break-glass path for supplier access is live.

options.label: Leave access in place, monitor it closely
options.description: Accept the access, but make sure you would see it being misused.
visibleKnownEffects: You are detecting rather than preventing

immediateEffects.reason: You did not disrupt operations.

options.label: Leave it for now
options.description: There are bigger problems this quarter.

decisions.title: The legacy warehouse platform
decisions.description: Meridian runs on unsupported software and cannot be patched. It supports despatch across three sites. Retirement is planned but repeatedly slips.
decisions.context: The COO cannot lose despatch. The CIO owns the migration that keeps slipping. Neither will thank you for a decision that makes their year harder.
decisions.teaches: Accepting risk is legitimate. Accepting it without recording the assumptions behind it is not.

options.label: Isolate it properly
options.description: Fund a containment project: strict network controls around the platform until it retires.
visibleKnownEffects: Integration work for the operations team
Meaningfully reduces what a compromise could reach

immediateEffects.reason: You added constraints around the warehouse platform.

delayedEffects.note: Containment around the legacy warehouse platform is in place.

options.label: Push to accelerate retirement
options.description: Take the argument to the CIO: the platform has to go this year, not next.
visibleKnownEffects: Depends entirely on the migration programme
Costs you credit with the CIO

immediateEffects.reason: You pushed on a migration date he does not control.

options.label: Accept until retirement, with compensating controls
options.description: Accept the exposure until the platform is retired, with monitoring in the meantime.
visibleKnownEffects: Depends on the retirement date holding

options.label: Fund a manual fulfilment fallback
options.description: Rather than protect the platform, make its loss survivable.
visibleKnownEffects: Materially reduces what an outage costs

immediateEffects.reason: You funded a fallback operations could actually use.

decisions.title: The repeat audit finding
decisions.description: External audit has raised privileged access management for the third consecutive year. The CFO wants to know what you are going to do about it.
decisions.context: The board has seen this finding before. How you respond shapes whether they believe the fourth year will be different.

options.label: Commit to a funded programme with dates
options.description: Tell audit and the board that this is being fixed properly, and commit to milestones.
visibleKnownEffects: You will be held to the dates
Meeting them means funding and staffing a programme

immediateEffects.reason: You gave audit a credible, dated answer.

options.label: Produce a remediation plan
options.description: The standard response: a plan, an owner and a target date.
visibleKnownEffects: So did the last two plans

options.label: Reframe the finding around business consequence
options.description: Accept the finding, but re-present it to the board as what it would actually cost rather than as a control gap.

immediateEffects.reason: You translated an audit finding into a business consequence.

decisions.title: The SOC contract renewal
decisions.description: Sentinel SOC's contract renews shortly. Procurement wants a decision. The service is cheap, the escalation quality is poor, and the coverage gaps are yours, not theirs.
decisions.context: Replacing a SOC provider takes six months and a great deal of your team's attention.

options.label: Renew as-is
options.description: Keep the service and spend your energy elsewhere.

immediateEffects.reason: You renewed without reopening the contract.

options.label: Renew with a rewritten scope
options.description: Same provider, different service: use cases tied to Nexora's attack paths, and escalation quality measured.
visibleKnownEffects: Takes about ten weeks to take effect

immediateEffects.reason: You reopened a contract schedule mid-cycle.

delayedEffects.note: The rewritten SOC scope is now in effect.

options.label: Go to market for a replacement
options.description: Start a procurement for a different provider.
visibleKnownEffects: The SOC is a person down for five months

delayedEffects.note: The new monitoring provider is fully live.

decisions.title: Connecting the acquisition
decisions.description: Kestrel Digital completes shortly. Integration wants to join its network to Nexora's corporate network on day one.
decisions.context: The CFO owns the deal timetable. Nobody has examined Kestrel's estate in any depth.
decisions.teaches: Integration deadlines and security conditions are usually negotiable together, not separately.

options.label: Connect on schedule
options.description: Do not be the reason the deal timetable slips.
visibleKnownEffects: You inherit whatever is already in their estate

immediateEffects.reason: You did not delay the acquisition.

options.label: Connect through a quarantined zone first
options.description: Join the estates, but keep Kestrel behind a controlled boundary until it has been examined.
visibleKnownEffects: Integration is slower and more expensive
Contains what you have not yet seen

immediateEffects.reason: You added cost and time to the integration.

options.label: Refuse connection until due diligence is done
options.description: No network join until someone has actually looked.

immediateEffects.reason: You blocked the integration.
You delayed value from the acquisition.

decisions.title: Finance asks for the cyber budget back
decisions.description: The cost reduction programme needs a contribution. Finance has asked for £220k from the cyber budget, or a named line worth half of it. If the money is not there, they will take what is.
decisions.context: Saying no costs credit. Saying yes costs capability. A smaller contribution from a named line is harder to argue for, and requires you to know your own plan well enough to name one.

options.label: Give it up
options.description: Take the cut and reprioritise.
visibleKnownEffects: Less is left for whatever comes up later

immediateEffects.note: Budget returned to the cost programme.

immediateEffects.reason: You contributed to the cost programme without a fight.

options.label: Refuse, and explain what it would cost
options.description: Set out precisely which capability would not be delivered.
visibleKnownEffects: The CFO will remember at the next budget round

immediateEffects.reason: You refused to contribute to the cost programme.

options.label: Offer a smaller contribution from a specific line
options.description: Give back what you can name, and protect what you cannot.
visibleKnownEffects: Requires you to know your own plan well

immediateEffects.note: Partial contribution to the cost programme.

immediateEffects.reason: You made a specific, defensible offer.

decisions.title: An executive exception request
decisions.description: Three senior leaders have asked to be exempted from the new privileged access flow. Their assistants cannot work with session recording.
decisions.context: Exceptions are how good controls quietly become partial controls.

options.label: Grant the exceptions
options.description: Keep the peace.

immediateEffects.reason: You were pragmatic about executive access.

options.label: Refuse
options.description: The control applies to everyone or it applies to no one.
visibleKnownEffects: Three senior people will be annoyed

immediateEffects.reason: You refused an executive exception.

options.label: Redesign the flow so the exception is unnecessary
options.description: Spend the engineering effort to make the control workable for delegated access.

delayedEffects.note: The redesigned privileged access flow is live; the executive exceptions have lapsed.

decisions.title: A working exploit for the checkout framework
decisions.description: A public exploit exists for the framework version running the checkout service. The delivery team's next release window is in eleven days.
decisions.context: Priya will not want an emergency change during the launch run-up. The alternative is carrying a known, weaponised weakness on an internet-facing service.

options.label: Force an emergency patch
options.description: Invoke emergency change and patch this week.

immediateEffects.reason: You forced an emergency change during the launch run-up.

options.label: Wait for the scheduled window
options.description: Eleven days is not long.
visibleKnownEffects: Eleven days of exposure to a public exploit

delayedEffects.note: The checkout framework has been patched in the scheduled window.

options.label: Mitigate at the edge, patch in the window
options.description: Block the exploit path at the perimeter now and patch on schedule.
visibleKnownEffects: Mitigation is not the same as a fix

delayedEffects.note: Checkout has been patched; the edge mitigation is retired.

decisions.title: Out-of-hours vendor access
decisions.description: The SOC has flagged vendor remote access sessions at 03:40 on three consecutive nights, outside the provider's contracted hours. Confidence is low.
decisions.context: This is exactly the kind of signal that is usually nothing, and occasionally is the only warning anyone gets.
decisions.teaches: Investigating costs real resources. So does not investigating.

options.label: Commission a focused threat hunt
options.description: Put the SOC team on it properly for a week.
visibleKnownEffects: Costs SOC capacity you may want later
Most likely outcome is that it was nothing

options.label: Ask the provider to explain it
options.description: Cheap, fast, and depends entirely on the provider being both honest and informed.
visibleKnownEffects: Tells you what the provider believes, not what happened

options.label: Suspend vendor access until it is explained
options.description: Close the route now, ask questions afterwards.

immediateEffects.note: Vendor remote access is suspended; whoever was using it at night is locked out.

immediateEffects.reason: You suspended supplier access with no notice.

options.label: Note it and keep watching
options.description: Low confidence, high volume, limited capacity.

decisions.title: Customer data held beyond policy
decisions.description: Records for closed accounts are retained indefinitely in the analytics estate. Legal is uncomfortable. The analytics team says the data is commercially valuable.
decisions.context: Ruth Ahmadi will support you if the facts are clear. The Insight Services business will not.

options.label: Enforce the retention policy
options.description: Delete what should not be there.
visibleKnownEffects: Materially reduces what a breach would expose

immediateEffects.reason: You enforced the retention policy.
You deleted data the analytics business wanted.

options.label: Restrict access rather than delete
options.description: Keep the data, and cut everyone who can read it down to a governed few.
visibleKnownEffects: The data still exists to be taken

options.label: Defer until after the launch
options.description: There is too much happening this quarter.
visibleKnownEffects: The data stays where it is
Legal will remember that you deferred it

immediateEffects.reason: You deferred a regulatory exposure she had raised.

decisions.title: Five vacancies and a long recruitment cycle
decisions.description: Two roles have been open for over six months. Recruitment takes about two months when it works.
decisions.context: The team is carrying the gap. That is not free, and it is not sustainable.

options.label: Recruit properly
options.description: Take the time to hire the right people.

delayedEffects.note: A new identity engineer has joined.

options.label: Bring in contractors now
options.description: Buy capacity immediately at a premium.
visibleKnownEffects: Expensive, and it leaves when the money stops

delayedEffects.note: The contractors have rolled off and taken their knowledge with them.

options.label: Hold the vacancies and protect the budget
options.description: Keep the money for programme delivery.

decisions.title: A material risk the board has not heard about
decisions.description: You are holding a risk assessment the board has never seen: {{unseenRisk}}. The next scheduled meeting is {{nextBoard}}.
decisions.context: Sir Alan Whitcombe's stated concern is whether management knows what it does not know. He is more forgiving of bad news than of late news.

options.label: Brief the risk chair now, out of cycle
options.description: Do not let him find out from the papers.
visibleKnownEffects: He will not be surprised later

immediateEffects.reason: You briefed him before he had to ask.
You went to the board chair before finishing the conversation with her.

options.label: Brief the CEO first, then the board together
options.description: Respect the reporting line, accept the delay.

immediateEffects.reason: You brought her the bad news first.

options.label: Wait for the scheduled meeting
options.description: It will be on the next agenda.

delayedEffects.note: The risk committee minutes record that a material risk reached them late, and by the scheduled route rather than when it was known.

decisions.title: Incident command
decisions.description: An incident is running. The question is whether you stand up formal incident command, with the disruption that brings, or manage it through the existing line.
decisions.context: Standing up command costs operational normality across the business. Not standing it up costs coordination when you most need it.

options.label: Stand up incident command now
options.description: Formal command, executive cadence, single decision path.

immediateEffects.reason: You took visible control of the incident.

options.label: Manage it through the line
options.description: Keep it contained within security operations for now.

decisions.title: Cut the actor off
decisions.description: The actor is still reaching in from outside. Cutting external access stops them, and it stops every supplier and remote worker who depends on that access too.
decisions.context: Operations depends on that access. So, for now, does the actor.

options.label: Cut all external access immediately
options.description: Everything external goes now.

immediateEffects.reason: You cut external access, suppliers included, during an incident with no warning.

options.label: Cut only the implicated accounts
options.description: Targeted, if you have identified the right accounts.
visibleKnownEffects: Depends on your identification being right

options.label: Keep access open and watch
options.description: Observe the actor rather than alerting them.

decisions.title: External response support
decisions.description: Your team is running the incident. Specialist external support would help, and there is no retainer in place.
decisions.context: Procuring response support during an incident is expensive and slow, but the alternative is your own people going without sleep.

options.label: Bring in external response support
options.description: Pay the emergency rate.
visibleKnownEffects: Emergency rates, payable whether or not the budget can meet them

options.label: Run it in-house
options.description: Your team handles it.

decisions.title: Regulatory notification
decisions.description: Customer data may have left the environment. The notification clock is either running or about to start.
decisions.context: Ruth Ahmadi needs a decision, and she needs the facts to be straight before it is made.

options.label: Notify early, on incomplete facts
options.description: Notify the regulator now and update as you learn more.
visibleKnownEffects: You may be correcting yourself publicly

immediateEffects.reason: You notified promptly.

options.label: Establish the facts first
options.description: Take the time to know what you are reporting.

effects.reason: Notification went out later than she was comfortable with.

delayedEffects.note: Legal has flagged the notification timing.

decisions.title: Take the platform down
decisions.description: The affected platform is still running. Taking it offline stops the damage spreading and stops the business with it.
decisions.context: The COO will want a number: how long. You do not have one.

options.label: Take it offline
options.description: Stop it now.

immediateEffects.reason: You took the platform down without a restoration estimate.

options.label: Keep it running while you contain
options.description: Contain around it rather than stopping it.

decisions.title: After the incident
decisions.description: The incident is closed. What you do with it now determines whether the organisation learns anything.
decisions.context: This is the moment the organisation is most willing to change, and least willing to hear that it was predictable.

options.label: Present what happened honestly, including what you chose not to do
options.description: Show what is known of how it happened, the controls that mattered, and the decisions, including yours.

immediateEffects.reason: You presented your own decisions in the incident reconstruction.

options.label: Produce a standard post-incident report
options.description: Facts, timeline, actions.

options.label: Use it to fund the programme
options.description: Take the moment and ask for what you needed before it happened.

immediateEffects.reason: You used the incident to reopen the budget.

decisions.title: Penetration test scope
decisions.description: The annual test is being scoped. The legacy estate was excluded last year on cost grounds.
decisions.context: The part of the estate least likely to pass is the part nobody wants in scope.

options.label: Include the legacy estate
options.description: Test the part you understand least.

delayedEffects.note: The penetration test report is in. The legacy estate was in scope, and it shows.

options.label: Keep the existing scope
options.description: Cloud and corporate, as before.
visibleKnownEffects: Another clean report about the same half of the estate

options.label: Run an assumed-breach test instead
options.description: Start the testers inside and see how far they get.
visibleKnownEffects: Tests detection as well as prevention

delayedEffects.note: The assumed-breach test report is in.

decisions.title: The HR provider's incident
decisions.description: People Cloud has disclosed unauthorised access to a support system. Your exposure is unconfirmed and they are being vague.
decisions.context: Employee data, an unclear disclosure, and a supplier who would prefer this went away.

options.label: Press them for specifics
options.description: Formal request, contractual footing, named questions.
visibleKnownEffects: You will get an answer, eventually

immediateEffects.reason: You pursued the provider's disclosure properly.

delayedEffects.note: The HR provider has confirmed the scope of its incident.

options.label: Wait for their next update
options.description: They have promised more information.

decisions.title: Your team is past sustainable load
decisions.description: Your leadership team has told you plainly that {{pressedFunction}} cannot carry the work it has been given.
decisions.context: Whatever you stop comes off {{pressedFunction}}, because that is where the load is. Money already spent on it stays spent; the delay is the cost.

options.label: Stop something
options.description: Pull work back and accept the delay.
visibleKnownEffects: The newest enquiry on that function is abandoned, or failing that its newest programme is paused
The load comes off; what it would have delivered, it will not

options.label: Buy capacity
options.description: Spend budget to relieve the pressure.

options.label: Ask them to push through the quarter
options.description: It is only a few more weeks.
visibleKnownEffects: It is never only a few more weeks

delayedEffects.note: Somebody senior on the part of the team you asked to push through has resigned.

decisions.title: Card data outside the payment environment
decisions.description: Unencrypted card data has been found in application logs outside the defined payment environment. Our card-acquiring bank does not know.
decisions.context: This is a compliance question and a risk question, and they have different answers.

options.label: Fix it and tell the card-acquiring bank
options.description: Remediate and disclose the scope issue.
visibleKnownEffects: Nobody can say you concealed it

immediateEffects.reason: You disclosed the payment scope issue.
You invited scrutiny from the card-acquiring bank.

options.label: Fix it quietly
options.description: Remediate without a formal disclosure.
visibleKnownEffects: It will be found at the next assessment

effects.reason: The payment scope issue surfaced at assessment rather than from you.

delayedEffects.note: The payment scope issue has surfaced during assessment.

decisions.title: Two programmes, one team
decisions.description: Both the identity and segmentation programmes need the same architecture capacity. Running both properly is not possible this quarter.
decisions.context: Choosing is the job. Running both at half staffing is how neither gets delivered.

options.label: Prioritise identity
options.description: Concentrate the capacity where most attack paths converge.

options.label: Prioritise segmentation
options.description: Concentrate on limiting what any single compromise can reach.

options.label: Run both at reduced pace
options.description: Keep both alive.
visibleKnownEffects: Nobody has to be told no

decisions.title: An acceptance has run out
decisions.description: The acceptance you recorded on {{scenario}} has reached the end of the period you gave it. You gave it on a stated rationale and a set of assumptions that were true then.
decisions.context: Renewing is a decision, not a default. The assumptions beneath the last one were made in a different quarter; if they still hold, say so and why. If you are not sure, that is the answer.

options.label: Renew it for another quarter
options.description: Carry it again, on the rationale you record now.
visibleKnownEffects: Ninety days, then this question again
The annual review reads the rationale against what happens

options.label: Look at it again before deciding
options.description: Bring the assessment current and put it back on the open register until you have.

options.label: Let it sit on the open register
options.description: Neither renew nor reassess: it is open, and it waits.
visibleKnownEffects: It is on your list until you do something

decisions.title: Make the identity controls mandatory
decisions.description: Identity and privileged access uplift is done, or as near as makes no difference. The vault and the second factor are built; what was never decided is whether they are mandatory. Engineering wants enforcement switched on now, freeze or no freeze. Operations wants it after peak trading.
decisions.context: Every week the control stays optional, the exception list grows, and an exception list is what an attacker reads first. Every week it is mandatory in peak trading is a week somebody senior is locked out.

options.label: Enforce now
options.description: Standing exceptions expire. Anyone without the second factor is locked out until they enrol.
visibleKnownEffects: Peak-trading teams lose a day or two
The control means what it says

immediateEffects.reason: You enforced the identity controls going into peak trading.

options.label: Phase it in after peak trading
options.description: Enforce in January. Hold exceptions at today's level until then.
visibleKnownEffects: The window between now and then is the one an attacker would choose

options.label: Leave enrolment voluntary
options.description: The programme completes. The control applies to those who chose it.
visibleKnownEffects: The exception list becomes the estate

immediateEffects.reason: You kept the identity controls voluntary through peak trading.

decisions.title: The restore test needs an outage window
decisions.description: The recovery capability is built and has never been run against production. A full restore test needs a four-hour outage on Nexora Pay. Operations will not give you one in peak trading; a test in January is a test next year.
decisions.context: You can go into peak trading knowing, or assuming. The difference is four hours of payments.

options.label: Take the window now
options.description: Four hours of payments downtime, scheduled, with the COO's name on it.
visibleKnownEffects: You go into peak trading knowing

immediateEffects.reason: You took four hours of payments for a restore test.

options.label: Restore into the test tenancy instead
options.description: Prove the backups can be read and time the restore, without touching production.
visibleKnownEffects: Proves the backups, not the runbook

options.label: Defer the test to January
options.description: Nothing is disrupted. The capability goes into peak trading on paper.
visibleKnownEffects: You go into peak trading on an assumption

decisions.title: The platform has outgrown its recovery design
decisions.description: The customer platform is carrying three times the volume it was designed for at launch. The recovery design assumed the old estate: a restore now takes longer than the business can stand, and nobody has re-planned it since the launch.
decisions.context: This is a success producing an exposure. Priya wants growth; Helen wants the platform to stay up; both are right, and the money is yours.

options.label: Fund a resilience redesign now
options.description: Re-plan recovery for the platform as it is, not as it was launched.

immediateEffects.reason: You funded resilience for the platform's growth.

delayedEffects.note: The platform recovery redesign is done; engineering has its people back.

options.label: Carry it until next year's plan
options.description: Record the assumption and take it to the budget round.
visibleKnownEffects: You are relying on the platform not failing in peak

options.label: Hold growth until the design catches up
options.description: Ask Digital to stop adding load until recovery is re-planned.

immediateEffects.reason: You asked Digital to hold the platform's growth.
You put a brake on the platform's growth.

decisions.title: Next year's budget after a quiet year
decisions.description: No incident reached the business this year. Finance is building next year's plan on a fifth less for cyber, and the argument for the current line is hard to make when the year had no incident to point at.
decisions.context: A quiet year is an outcome. Whether it was capability or fortune is the question the cut assumes an answer to, and the only evidence either way is what you verified.

options.label: Accept the cut
options.description: Take the fifth off and reprioritise next year.

immediateEffects.reason: You accepted the cut to next year's cyber budget.

options.label: Make the case with what you verified
options.description: Argue that the quiet was capability, and show the board what you checked.
visibleKnownEffects: The board hears why quiet is not the same as safe

immediateEffects.reason: You refused the cut to next year's cyber budget.

options.label: Offer a named line instead
options.description: Give back what you can name, and protect what you cannot.
visibleKnownEffects: You keep what you can explain

immediateEffects.reason: You offered a smaller, named cut.

decisions.title: Corvus renewal: whose terms?
decisions.description: Corvus Managed Services renews in January and the contract goes to signature in December. Whatever was decided about their access this year lives in emails and change records, not in the contract.
decisions.context: A contract term outlives the people who agreed it. Nadia Farrell will write in anything specific; Helen Brandt will read every clause for what it does to night cover.

options.label: Write the access terms into the contract
options.description: Requested, time-bound and recorded access becomes a contractual obligation, with the right to audit how their engineers connect.

immediateEffects.reason: You gave procurement terms specific enough to write down.

options.label: Renew on last year's paper
options.description: Sign what was signed last year and keep the access arrangements informal.
visibleKnownEffects: The contract still permits standing access

options.label: Take it to tender
options.description: Test the market for a provider whose way of working does not depend on standing access.
visibleKnownEffects: Procurement effort through the first quarter
Operations will worry about night cover

immediateEffects.reason: You put the night-cover provider out to tender in peak trading.
You asked procurement to test the market.

decisions.title: Lifting the Kestrel quarantine
decisions.description: Kestrel Digital has sat behind a controlled boundary since the network join. Integration wants it lifted before year end so the synergy savings land in this year's accounts.
decisions.context: The boundary contains whatever is in Kestrel's estate, examined or not. The CFO owns the number; you own what comes through when it goes.

options.label: Lift it now
options.description: Let the savings land this year.
visibleKnownEffects: Kestrel's estate joins the corporate network

immediateEffects.reason: You lifted the quarantine in time for the year's numbers.

options.label: Lift it after a scoped review
options.description: Two weeks of architecture time on what crosses the boundary, then lift it.

immediateEffects.reason: The quarantine outlasted this year's accounts.

options.label: Hold it until January
options.description: Keep the boundary through peak trading and decide in the new year.

immediateEffects.reason: You held the Kestrel quarantine past year end.

decisions.title: The audit follow-up
decisions.description: External audit returns for the year-end follow-up on privileged access, and will test the dates you committed to early in the year against production.
decisions.context: The finding has been raised three years running. Closing it depends on what is running, not on what is planned.

options.label: Show them production as it is
options.description: Walk the auditors through what is enforced today, including what is not.
visibleKnownEffects: The finding may stay open another year
Nothing you say can be contradicted

immediateEffects.reason: You showed the auditors production as it is.
The privileged access finding may stay open another year.

options.label: Present the programme as on track
options.description: Lead with the plan and the milestones reached.
visibleKnownEffects: Rests on the programme being where you say

immediateEffects.reason: You gave the auditors a confident account.

options.label: Ask for the finding to be re-scoped
options.description: Argue that the finding should cover privileged access to production only.
visibleKnownEffects: Audit will read it as moving the goalposts

immediateEffects.reason: You asked audit to narrow a finding you had committed to closing.

decisions.title: Next year's priorities, in writing
decisions.description: The board risk committee wants three priorities for next year, and what you will not do, in writing before the January meeting.
decisions.context: Sir Alan Whitcombe will read what you write now against everything the committee has heard from you this year.

options.label: Lead with the risks you raised
options.description: Three open risks from your register, each with what it would take to move it.
visibleKnownEffects: Consistent with what the board has heard

immediateEffects.reason: Your priorities matched the risks you had brought him.

options.label: Lead with the programmes you are running
options.description: Next year as the continuation of this year's delivery plan.
visibleKnownEffects: Says what you are doing, not why

requirements.conditionUnmet: You are not running a programme to lead with

immediateEffects.reason: Your priorities were costed and already in the plan.

options.label: Lead with what you still do not know
options.description: Three questions the organisation cannot yet answer, and what it would cost to answer them.
visibleKnownEffects: The board sees where the uncertainty is

immediateEffects.reason: You put what you do not know in writing.
Your priorities paper led with uncertainty.

decisions.title: They are back in touch
decisions.description: Last quarter's attackers say they still hold customer records taken before the encryption, and want paying to delete them. They have sent a sample of forty rows, and the rows are real.
decisions.context: Payment buys a promise from criminals. Silence buys time, until they publish. Notification tells the regulator something you cannot yet fully describe.

options.label: Refuse, and notify the regulator
options.description: Tell the regulator and the board what you know and what you do not, before the attackers can.
visibleKnownEffects: Nobody can say you hid it

immediateEffects.reason: You notified before anyone could say you had hidden it.
You told the board about the extortion before it became news.

options.label: Refuse, and say nothing unless they publish
options.description: Do not pay, do not notify, and wait to see whether they follow through.
visibleKnownEffects: If they publish, it looks like concealment

options.label: Pay to have it deleted
options.description: Pay from the cyber budget, through a negotiator, against a promise of deletion.
visibleKnownEffects: Buys a promise, not a guarantee

immediateEffects.reason: You paid criminals out of the cyber budget.
The board learned you had paid an extortion demand.

decisions.title: The board wants something it can see
decisions.description: A board member has seen a vendor's detection platform demonstrated and wants the new money to buy something the committee can point at. The platform is good. It is also £300k and months of engineering to deploy properly.
decisions.context: Visible spend buys the board's patience. Invisible spend buys capability the board cannot see until something does not happen.

options.label: Buy the flagship platform
options.description: Buy it, announce it, and deploy what the team can alongside everything else.
visibleKnownEffects: The board has something to point at
Engineering has another thing to deploy

immediateEffects.reason: You gave the committee something it could see.

options.label: Put the money into the programmes
options.description: Tell the board the money is going into delivery, and let delivery speak.
visibleKnownEffects: Nothing new to show the committee
The money goes where the plan says

immediateEffects.reason: The committee had nothing new to see for the money.
You spent the increase on the plan rather than a purchase.

options.label: Show them the plan instead
options.description: Take the committee through what the money will buy and when they will be able to see it.

decisions.title: Your predecessor's numbers
decisions.description: The multi-factor coverage figure in last year's board papers counted staff accounts only. Service accounts, partner accounts and the supplier's engineers were never in it. The number was true of what it measured.
decisions.context: The board has been told a figure for a year. Correcting it is honest and expensive; not correcting it makes it yours.

options.label: Restate the figure to the board
options.description: Put the corrected number in front of the committee, with what it now covers and what it does not.
visibleKnownEffects: The board hears a worse number
You own the figure from now on

immediateEffects.reason: You corrected your predecessor's figure yourself.

options.label: Correct it quietly in the next paper
options.description: Report the right number from now on without drawing attention to the change.
visibleKnownEffects: Someone may notice the number moved

options.label: Leave it: it was your predecessor's figure
options.description: Carry the number as reported and revisit it when you have your own.
visibleKnownEffects: The figure becomes yours by default
